draft.exec:
Kirana Logistics runs its applications on AWS but asked for a managed MySQL in Alibaba Cloud Jakarta for data residency. Separating the database from the applications risks slower queries or dropped connections if the link between them is unreliable.

This proposal places a managed MySQL database in Jakarta and connects it to your AWS application servers over a dedicated private line.

Your data stays in Jakarta while your applications continue running where they are today. Confirming the expected traffic volume between AWS and Jakarta unlocks the sizing of that link.

needs.need: AWS applications must reach the Jakarta database securely.
needs.answer: A dedicated private line carries database queries between AWS and Jakarta, keeping traffic off the public internet and reducing exposure to interception or disruption.

needs.need: MySQL data must stay in Jakarta.
needs.quote: managed MySQL in Alibaba Cloud Jakarta for data residency
needs.answer: The design hosts the database in Jakarta so records remain there, meeting your stated goal while your applications continue operating on AWS.

outcomes.title: Private cross-cloud connectivity
outcomes.text: A dedicated line links AWS applications to the Jakarta database, keeping query traffic off the public internet and reducing exposure to external disruption.

outcomes.title: Cost shape across clouds
outcomes.text: The managed database shifts maintenance effort from your team to the provider. The cross-cloud link is a fixed commitment, while database compute scales with actual query load.

why.rds: Kirana Logistics asked for managed MySQL in Jakarta for data residency. ApsaraDB RDS keeps the data in Jakarta across two zones with built-in backups, reducing outage risk and the operational effort your team spends on database maintenance.
why.express-connect: Your AWS applications need a reliable path to the Jakarta database. Express Connect provides a dedicated physical line for that traffic, reducing the risk of latency spikes or exposure that come with routing queries over the public internet.

tradeoffs.text: Database queries travel between AWS and Jakarta over a dedicated line, adding network latency compared to a local setup.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Confirm the expected traffic volume so the link capacity matches demand without overspending.

tradeoffs.text: The design assumes the dedicated line meets your security requirements for cross-cloud data transit.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Review the connection model with your security team before provisioning.

next: Schedule a cost-estimate session with the account team once the traffic band is confirmed.
Confirm whether steady traffic between AWS and Jakarta falls under 1 Gbps, between 1 and 10 Gbps, or over 10 Gbps.
Share your preferred start date for provisioning the Jakarta database and the cross-cloud link.
